author: golden state today
title: Rep. Norma Torres addresses immigration justice and law enforcement accountability in recent posts
text:
Rep. Norma Torres, who represents California’s 35th district in the U.S. Congress, recently posted a series of statements on her social media account addressing issues related to immigrant rights, law enforcement accountability, and honoring a fallen deputy.
On November 18, 2025, Torres wrote in Spanish: “He visto la crueldad de los centros de detención de Trump. Sigo luchando y seguire luchando por justicia y dignidad para los inmigrantes en los centros, en los tribunales y en su vida diaria.” This post highlights her ongoing advocacy for justice and dignity for immigrants in detention centers and beyond.
Later that day, Torres paid tribute to Deputy Nuñez with the following message: “Today, we mourn the loss of Deputy Nuñez: husband, father, son, and hero. He gave his life protecting our community, and his sacrifice will never be forgotten. To his family, loved ones, and fellow officers: we stand with you. Deputy Nuñez’s legacy of courage and service lives”. Her remarks acknowledged the officer’s service and expressed solidarity with his family and colleagues.
In another post on November 18, 2025, Torres commented on federal law enforcement practices in California: “Impunity is not acceptable. California is right: Federal agents who hide their identities to abuse power and break the law are getting away with it. The DOJ’s lawsuit is NOT about ‘officer safety.’ It’s about shielding corruption. We must demand transparency and hold those in”.
Norma Torres has served as a member of Congress since 2015 after succeeding Gloria Negrete McLeod. She previously held positions in both the California State Assembly from 2008 to 2013 and the California Senate from 2013 to 2014. Born in Escuintla, Guatemala in 1965, Torres resides in Pomona and holds a Bachelor of Arts degree from National Labor College.
